pages.title: payments: notes for on-call
facts: Duplicate capture on 63 bookings on 2026-01-14: the capture call to stripe was retried after a timeout and both captures went through. Leo added an idempotency key to the capture call on 2026-01-15. Mei's team refunded the second charge the same day.
The weekly payout job runs on Sunday at 23:00 JST and usually takes about 38 minutes.
Refund batches run daily at 23:30 JST.
Webhooks from the card provider can arrive late, out of order, or more than once; payments is built to handle all three, so a few retries are not an incident.

pages.title: notifier: things we learned the hard way
facts: After the sending-domain switch on 2026-02-24, sendgrid's suppression list picked up 2,312 addresses from soft bounces during the switch, and sendgrid stopped sending to them. Yuki checked they were valid and removed them from the suppression list on 2026-02-26.
The nightly reminder batch (02:00 to 04:00 JST) regularly pushes queue depth past 1,000; check delivered per minute before treating it as a stall.
Email confirmations and SMS reminders use separate queues.
Every reminder carries a dedupe key, reminder:<booking id>:<date>; notifier drops a message whose key it has seen in the last 24 hours.

pages.title: web: odd things we keep seeing
facts: Tofu on the booking page in June 2026: customer names with rare kanji (for example 髙 or 﨑) rendered as empty boxes, because the subset web font left out those glyphs. Priya added a fallback to the full Noto Sans JP font on 2026-06-11.
Search-engine crawler bursts on public business pages trip web-traffic a few times a month; they are harmless when 5xx and page load stay flat.
Safari keeps the old service worker longer than other browsers; after a release, support can ask a customer to reload twice.
The cloudflare edge serves most static files; a purge normally finishes in about a minute.
